newsitem.title: FRANCE: France authorises gene-maize marketing - decree.
newsitem.headline: France authorises gene-maize marketing - decree.

text.p: France has cleared the marketing of gene-modified maize, a decree published in the Wednesday edition of the Official Journal shows.
The farm ministry decree dated February 4 and published on February 5 authorises the marketing of the maize developed by the Swiss firm Ciba-Ceigy and adapted to resist the corn borer pest.
The move had been widely expected after France made on February 2 the labelling of gene-altered organisms and derived products mandatory.

In a statement released on February 3 the farm ministry specified that the marketing authorisation would apply only to "the import of maize and derived products" and not yet to the cultivation of gene-altered maize.

In December the European Union cleared imports of genetically-modified maize for sale in Europe but said it it would revise laws allowing for the labelling of goods containing gene-altered products. It is to issue labelling guidelines to EU member states by mid-March, a Commission's environmental spokesman said on Wednesday.

France had initially said it would approve the sale of gene-maize only when EU labelling rules were in place. But pressed by consumer and environmental groups concerned over possible risks to health and environment, it did not wait for the EU rules and issued its own labelling code.
